border.title: Border
border.summary: Colors an inside band along the edge of an input silhouette.
border.input: Connect a shape or an image whose alpha defines the silhouette.
border.output: A colored inside border that preserves the input silhouette.
border.usage: Set Width in document units and choose the border color. Connect a shape with distance data for the most direct result.
border.notes: Without usable distance, the border samples the alpha mask in a bounded neighborhood. Fine details below the sampling scale may be approximated, and wide borders cost more than an analytic distance band.

cell_data.title: Cell Data
cell_data.summary: Stable UV-grid or instance data: random values, indices, parity and hierarchical keys.
cell_data.input: No image is required. Instance scope reads the enclosing Grid through row and parameter connections.
cell_data.output: Random scalar/color, local UV, cell center, integer indices, parity, group random/key or cell key. Named center/size/angle fields expose the composed placement frame in placement-space units.
cell_data.usage: Use UV Grid for standalone periodic controls. Inside repeated rows choose Instance; connect Parity to a Transform rotation or random values to color/seed controls.
cell_data.notes: Instance scope uses stable current-instance data. Outside placement it uses a fixed zero key, rather than falling back to UV-grid randomness. Local UV follows transformations. Named fields can be selected directly on connections. Instance Center, Size and Angle describe the composed placement frame, avoiding references back to the parent row. This frame describes placement before nonlinear warps.

cells.title: Cells
cells.text: Positive integer cells per UV unit, rounded and clamped to 1–1024.

offset.title: Offset
offset.text: Offset in cell units. A half-cell offset changes where cell centers fall.

seed.title: Seed
seed.text: Deterministic seed. Nested Grids also hash the parent identity to keep subcells independent.

scope.title: Scope
scope.text: UV Grid derives cells from UV. Instance derives keys from placement and uses a fixed zero key outside an instance.

output.title: Output
output.text: Selects the control field supplied by this row.

circle.title: Circle
circle.summary: A circular shape with antialiased coverage and signed distance.
circle.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
circle.output: RGB is white and alpha carries antialiased shape coverage. Shape Distance is available as a separate connection choice.
circle.usage: Control Radius and Center, then use Color or another style row to color the silhouette. Connect coverage or a derived mask to Opacity when the shape should cut out the material.
circle.notes: Signed distance is negative inside and positive outside. Coarse material Height and surface color are separate from the shape distance.

center.title: Center
center.text: Center of the shape in document coordinates.

smoothness.title: Union Smoothness
smoothness.text: Blend width for Smooth Union with a preceding shape; it does not change a standalone shape.

color.title: Color
color.summary: Solid color across the image or within the incoming alpha mask. Preserves optional distance.
color.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
color.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
color.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
color.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

color_blend.title: Mix
color_blend.summary: Mixes two constant or connected RGBA endpoints using a per-channel factor.
color_blend.input: Optional image input supplies a mask and coverage; without it, only Factor controls interpolation.
color_blend.output: RGB interpolates per channel. Alpha interpolates with the mean clamped factor and multiplies input coverage.
color_blend.usage: Connect A and B, then Factor. To colorize a grayscale input like the former Color Blend, set Factor to (1, 1, 1).
color_blend.notes: Both endpoints and Factor accept row connections. Endpoints can carry their own alpha. Unbounded RGB factors allow extrapolation.

color1.title: A
color1.text: First endpoint, as constant RGBA or a connected row.

color2.title: B
color2.text: Second endpoint, as constant RGBA or a connected row.

factor.title: Factor
factor.text: Per-channel interpolation weight, multiplied by the optional image input. Zero selects A and one selects B.

compare_select.title: Compare/Select
compare_select.summary: Compares values to make a mask or select between two results.
compare_select.input: The image supplies the values being compared. Reference, True and False may be constants or other row connections.
compare_select.output: Mask returns comparison coverage. Select blends False and True using that coverage. RGB channels are compared separately.
compare_select.usage: Use Mask for material regions, or Select for crossing order and alternative colors. Softness smooths transitions; Tolerance defines the equality band.
compare_select.notes: Greater and Less exclude exact equality. Greater or Equal and Less or Equal include it. Connect the resulting mask to Opacity when it should remove material.

softness.title: Softness
softness.text: Half-width of the transition around the reference. Zero uses the exact comparison, including its behavior at equality.

tolerance.title: Tolerance
tolerance.text: Equal and Not Equal compare absolute difference with this tolerance. Softness adds a falloff outside the tolerance band.

directional_grain.title: Directional Grain
directional_grain.summary: Curved directional fibers with sparse grooves and a separate relief signal.
directional_grain.input: No image input is needed. Seed may be driven by cell or strip data.
directional_grain.output: Choose Grain, Grooves or Height. Packed returns Grain in X, Grooves in Y and Height in Z. Incoming alpha and optional distance are preserved.
directional_grain.usage: Set Direction and the along/across Scale values. Use per-strip seeds for wicker. Use Grain for subtle color variation, Grooves for wear masks, and Height for fine normals.
directional_grain.notes: Inside a Grid, UV follows instance orientation. Seed Scope can add stable Instance or Group variation. Axis-aligned integer scales repeat naturally; other directions may need seamless wrapping.

scale.title: Scale
scale.text: Along-grain and across-grain cell counts. Rounded and clamped to 1..1024.

direction.title: Direction
direction.text: Grain direction in degrees: zero is horizontal, 90 is vertical. Other angles may need seamless material wrapping.

seedScope.title: Seed Scope
seedScope.text: Fixed uses Seed alone. Instance and Group add a stable hash from the enclosing Grid identity.

bend.title: Bend
bend.text: Small fiber curvature, measured in across-grain cell units.

grooveWidth.title: Groove Width
grooveWidth.text: Groove width as a fraction of a fiber cell. Narrow filtered lines keep wear localized instead of creating broad noise patches.

disc.title: Disc
disc.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
disc.output: The preview shows the shape. Circle and Rounded Rectangle also provide signed distance as a separate connection choice; a grayscale shape result is not automatically material Opacity.
disc.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
disc.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

GRAD.title: Random Gradient
GRAD.text: Gives the shape a random gradient, useful for generating uneveness through visually tilting the shape.

globalScale.title: Global
globalScale.text: Global scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

localScale.title: Local
localScale.text: Local X/Y scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

offset.title: Offset
offset.text: X/Y offset of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the offset should be 0. as the pattern will position the shape automatically.

fbm.title: fBm
fbm.summary: Builds layered detail by sampling an input row at increasing frequencies.
fbm.input: Connect the noise or image row you want to layer. The same operation works with 2D and 3D sources.
fbm.output: The weighted RGB sum divided by the total octave weight. Incoming alpha is retained.
fbm.usage: Start with three to five Octaves. Increase Lacunarity for greater frequency separation or Gain for stronger fine detail. Select a single channel on the input connection when layering packed data.
fbm.notes: More octaves re-evaluate the entire upstream row and can be expensive. Unit-repeat behavior depends on the source and frequency multipliers. Organic fBm is a separate complete source preserving its own response.

layers.title: Octaves
layers.text: Number of layers. Each layer samples the connected row again.

lacunarity.title: Lacunarity
lacunarity.text: Frequency multiplier between layers. Two doubles the frequency at each octave.

gain.title: Gain
gain.text: Amplitude multiplier between layers. Lower values reduce fine detail.

globalScale.title: Scale
globalScale.text: Overall feature-size multiplier applied before sampling.

localScale.title: Stretch
localScale.text: Feature-size multipliers along the sampled axes.

gabor.title: Gabor Noise
gabor.summary: Localized directional wave packets for dunes, striations and banded detail.
gabor.input: No input image is required. Optional incoming alpha is preserved.
gabor.output: A signed wave sum repeated in RGB. It is not normalized into a guaranteed zero-to-one range.
gabor.usage: Adjust the blob count and size for coverage, and Frequency for stripe spacing. Use Levels, a profile, or Mix to turn the signed signal into material properties.
gabor.notes: More blobs increase evaluation cost. This source has its own character and should not be treated as interchangeable with smooth value noise.

height_to_normal.title: Height to Normal
height_to_normal.summary: Converts a height field into an encoded tangent-space normal map.
height_to_normal.input: Connect grayscale height, or select the required channel on the image connection.
height_to_normal.output: Encoded RGB normal: flat height produces approximately 0.5, 0.5, 1. Alpha and optional shape distance are preserved.
height_to_normal.usage: Connect the result to Normal Map. Use Strength to control relief and Radius to set the derivative sampling span.
height_to_normal.notes: Normal maps change lighting rather than geometry. Keep coarse form in Height when you need displacement. The derivative strength is independent of bake resolution, but very fine detail can still exceed that resolution.

strength.title: Strength
strength.text: Height-to-slope scale in UV units. Negative values invert the relief.

radius.title: Radius
radius.text: Derivative sampling radius in Pixels or UV units. Pixels retain the previous minimum of 0.5; small UV radii keep a physical sampling scale.

flipY.title: Flip Y
flipY.text: Off produces OpenGL-style tangent normals; enable to invert the green channel.

units.title: Units
units.text: Derivative radius in pixels or UV units. Pixels retain the previous default behavior.

mixer_divide.title: Divide
mixer_divide.summary: Divides each channel by a constant or connected vector.
mixer_divide.input: RGB dividend. Connect a Value row for a constant dividend.
mixer_divide.usage: Set Divisor or connect another row, using its channel selector when a scalar is needed.
mixer_divide.notes: Divisors closer to zero than 0.000001 use a signed epsilon.

multiply.title: Multiply
multiply.summary: The output is the result of the multiplication of the input value with the global and local properties.
multiply.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
multiply.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
multiply.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
multiply.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_abs.title: Abs
op_abs.summary: The output is the absolute / non-negative value of the input.
op_abs.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_abs.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_abs.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_abs.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_clamp.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.

op_cos.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_cos.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_cos.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_cos.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_floor.title: Floor

op_floor.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_floor.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_floor.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.

op_fract.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_fract.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_max.title: Max
op_max.summary: The output is the greater of the input value and the global property multiplied with the local property.
op_max.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_max.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_max.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_max.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_min.title: Min
op_min.summary: The output is the lesser of the input value and the global property multiplied with the local property.
op_min.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_min.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_min.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_min.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_oneminus.title: One Minus
op_oneminus.summary: The output is the result of the value property (by default one) minus the input value.
op_oneminus.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_oneminus.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_oneminus.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_oneminus.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_powproperty.title: Power
op_powproperty.summary: Raises nonnegative input channels to a constant or connected exponent.
op_powproperty.input: RGB bases. Connect a Value row for a constant base.
op_powproperty.usage: Exponent below one lifts dark values; above one tightens highlights.
op_powproperty.notes: Negative bases are clamped to zero. Zero bases use an epsilon for nonpositive exponents to keep results finite.

op_sign.title: Sign
op_sign.summary: The output is -1.0 if the input value is negative and 1.0 if it is positive, 0.0 otherwise.
op_sign.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_sign.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_sign.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_sign.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_sin.title: Sin
op_sin.summary: The output is the sine of the input value multiplied by the scale property.
op_sin.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_sin.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_sin.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_sin.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_smoothstep.title: Smooth Step
op_smoothstep.summary: The output is a smooth hermite interpolation between 0..1 if the input value is located between the lower and upper edge. 0.0 or 1.0 otherwise.
op_smoothstep.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_smoothstep.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_smoothstep.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_smoothstep.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_squareroot.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_squareroot.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.

op_squareroot.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

op_subtract.title: Subtract

op_subtract.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
op_subtract.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
op_subtract.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
op_subtract.notes: Select a single source channel when you want to process one field from a packed result. Choosing All channels processes the RGB components separately unless the tile says otherwise.

organic_fbm.title: Organic fBm
organic_fbm.summary: Dave Hoskins' matching layered organic noise, available as a complete source.
organic_fbm.input: No noise input is required. An optional preceding image can supply alpha coverage.
organic_fbm.output: The original weighted octave sum, capped at one and repeated in RGB.
organic_fbm.usage: Set Frequency for the broad structure, Octaves for detail, Gain for fine-detail strength, and Amplitude for overall contribution.
organic_fbm.notes: This preserves the matching organic fractal response, including its final cap at one. It is not normalized like general fBm. Large amplitudes can flatten bright areas. Integer Frequency maintains the intended unit repeat.

layers.title: Octaves
layers.text: Number of accumulated noise layers. More octaves add finer detail and increase evaluation cost.

amplitude.title: Amplitude
amplitude.text: Weight of the first octave. The final result is capped at one.

gain.title: Gain
gain.text: Weight multiplier from one octave to the next.

scaleValue.title: Frequency
scaleValue.text: Frequency of the first octave. Subsequent octaves double their frequency.

organic_noise.title: Organic Noise
organic_noise.summary: Dave Hoskins' organic, tileable value noise, with softly connected patches.
organic_noise.input: No image input is needed. Optional incoming alpha is preserved.
organic_noise.output: A scalar value repeated in RGB.
organic_noise.usage: Use Frequency to set the number of features. Feed the result to Mix, roughness, height, or a mask.
organic_noise.notes: Integer Frequency repeats over one UV unit. Fractional frequency can introduce seams. For the matching layered result, choose Organic fBm; connecting this source to a special fractal wrapper is unnecessary.

scaleValue.title: Frequency
scaleValue.text: Feature frequency. Larger values produce more, smaller features. Use an integer for a one-unit repeat.

pattern_brickandtiles_shape.title: Brick & Tiles (Pattern)
pattern_brickandtiles_shape.summary: Generates a brick or tile pattern. Needs an input shape or pattern (by default Tile). Returns the cell id in the X component, the depth map in Y and the angle of the shape in degrees in the Z component.
pattern_brickandtiles_shape.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
pattern_brickandtiles_shape.output: Packed layout data: X is a cell value, Y is height/depth, and Z is orientation in degrees. Select the field on each outgoing connection.
pattern_brickandtiles_shape.usage: Connect Tile or Disc as the legacy shape input where required. Read Height/Depth (Y) before colorizing; read X separately for cell variation.
pattern_brickandtiles_shape.notes: This is a specialized layout recipe. Its packed RGB output is not a ready-colored material, and its legacy shape inputs are not interchangeable with every modern alpha-mask shape.

inRatio.title: Ratio
inRatio.text: Width / height ratio of the individual shapes.

inGap.title: Gap
inGap.text: Gap between the shapes in percent.

inMaxRandRot.title: Max Rotation
inMaxRandRot.text: Maximum random rotation per shape in degrees. A value of 0 means no rotation, a value of 10 means each shape gets randomly rotated up to 10 degrees.

BRICK.title: Brick
BRICK.text: Switch between shape and brick pattern.

probability.title: Probability
probability.text: The probability that a given shape is drawn, 1. always draws every shape, lower values draw less and less shapes.

shapeN.title: Amount
shapeN.text: The amount of shapes in the x and y direction.

SUPERCELL.title: Grid
SUPERCELL.text: Shapes can be grouped into a grid. The grid gap will be applied after every x, y grid shape. Only applicable for tiles, not bricks.

SUPERGAP.title: Grid Gap
SUPERGAP.text: Shapes can be grouped into a grid. The grid gap will be applied after every x, y grid shape. Only applicable for tiles, not bricks.

pattern_checker.title: Checker B/W
pattern_checker.summary: Generates a simple b/w checkerboard pattern.
pattern_checker.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
pattern_checker.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
pattern_checker.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
pattern_checker.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

inRatio.title: Ratio

inGap.title: Gap

inHOLLOW.title: Center Size
inHOLLOW.text: The size of the empty center in shapes.

inMaxRandRot.title: Max Rotation

BRICK.title: Brick
BRICK.text: Switch between shape and brick pattern.

probability.title: Probability
probability.text: The probability that a given shape is drawn, 1. always draws every shape, lower values draw less and less shapes.

RANDofs.title: Random Offsets
RANDofs.text: Adds a random offset to the offsets between circles to reduce visible tiling.

shapeN.title: Amount
shapeN.text: The amount of shapes in the x and y direction.

pattern_decortiles_shape.title: Decor Tiles
pattern_decortiles_shape.summary: Generates a decor stone tile pattern. Needs an input shape (by default Tile). Returns the cell id in the x component, the depth map in y and the angle of the tiles in degrees in the z component.
pattern_decortiles_shape.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
pattern_decortiles_shape.output: Packed layout data: X is a cell value, Y is height/depth, and Z is orientation in degrees. Select the field on each outgoing connection.
pattern_decortiles_shape.usage: Connect Tile or Disc as the legacy shape input where required. Read Height/Depth (Y) before colorizing; read X separately for cell variation.
pattern_decortiles_shape.notes: This is a specialized layout recipe. Its packed RGB output is not a ready-colored material, and its legacy shape inputs are not interchangeable with every modern alpha-mask shape.

RATIO.title: Ratio
RATIO.text: Width / height ratio of the individual tiles.

inGap.title: Gap
inGap.text: Gap between the tiles in percent.

inMaxRandRot.title: Max Rotation
inMaxRandRot.text: Maximum random rotation per tile in degrees. A value of 0 means no rotation, a value of 10 means each tile gets randomly rotated up to 10 degrees.

shapeN.title: Amount
shapeN.text: The amount of shapes in the x and y direction.

pattern_fabricewood.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
pattern_fabricewood.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

fibers_A.title: Fibers Amplitude

LACUNARITY.text: The amount the shapes get smaller per layer.

RADIUS_D.title: Size Distribution
RADIUS_D.text: Size distribution of the cells. Higher values vary the size more.

AMP_D.title: Intensity Distribution
AMP_D.text: Intensity distribution of the cells. Higher values vary the intensity of cells more.

periodic_profile.title: Periodic Profile
periodic_profile.summary: Repeating one-dimensional profiles from a coordinate or control signal.
periodic_profile.input: Connect a coordinate channel. For horizontal strips, start from UV Y; for vertical strips, start from UV X.
periodic_profile.output: A rounded, dome, triangle or flat profile for each input component. Alpha and optional shape distance are preserved.
periodic_profile.usage: Choose a Profile, adjust Width for the filled portion of each repeat, and Phase for its position. Multiply coordinates upstream to control repeat density.
periodic_profile.notes: Antialiasing filters the profile over the estimated input footprint. This makes narrow repeated profiles more stable when viewed at a distance.

frequency.title: Frequency
frequency.text: Cycles per input unit. Negative frequencies reverse the profile; zero produces a constant phase.

width.title: Width
width.text: Occupied fraction of each period. Zero is empty; one fills the period.

phase.title: Phase
phase.text: Phase offset in cycles. Peaks are centered at integer input coordinates when phase is zero.

antialias.title: Antialias
antialias.text: Integrates the selected profile over the local input footprint. Unresolved repeats converge to their mean instead of flickering.

perlin.title: Perlin Noise
perlin.summary: Smooth gradient noise for broad variation and layered surface detail.
perlin.input: No image input is required. An optional input carries shape coverage through the noise.
perlin.output: The same scalar noise value is returned in RGB. Incoming alpha is preserved.
perlin.usage: Start with Scale, then stretch X and Y for elongated features. Select 3D to sample a position-based volume; Z Slice changes the slice shown in the material preview.
perlin.notes: Larger Scale values make larger features. Ordinary Perlin is not a guaranteed one-unit repeat; use Seamless material wrapping when required.

globalScale.title: Scale
globalScale.text: Feature size. Increasing Scale enlarges the pattern.

localScale.title: Stretch XY
localScale.text: Feature-size multipliers along X and Y.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.text: 2D uses UV coordinates. 3D uses position coordinates and the selected Z slice.

slice.title: Z Slice
slice.text: Position of the sampled plane along Z. Used in 3D mode.

depthScale.title: Stretch Z
depthScale.text: Feature-size multiplier along Z. Used in 3D mode.

rounded_rectangle.title: Rounded Rectangle
rounded_rectangle.summary: A rectangular shape with rounded corners, antialiased coverage and signed distance.
rounded_rectangle.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
rounded_rectangle.output: RGB is white and alpha carries antialiased shape coverage. Shape Distance is available as a separate connection choice.
rounded_rectangle.usage: Use Half Size for half the brick or strip width and height, and Corner Radius to soften corners. Build bevel or height profiles from Shape Distance rather than covering the form with broad noise.
rounded_rectangle.notes: Corner radius is limited by the smaller half-size. The shape does not repeat itself; layout and shape creation are separate operations.

halfSize.title: Half Size
halfSize.text: Half of the rectangle width and height, measured from its center.

radius.title: Corner Radius
radius.text: Radius of rounded corners, limited by the smaller half-size.

center.title: Center
center.text: Center of the shape in document coordinates.

smoothness.title: Union Smoothness
smoothness.text: Blend width for Smooth Union with a preceding shape; it does not change a standalone shape.

shape2d_polygon.title: Polygon
shape2d_polygon.summary: A regular or seeded irregular polygon with negative-inside signed edge distance.
shape2d_polygon.input: Optional incoming shape for shape combinations.
shape2d_polygon.output: RGBA coverage and an exact signed distance while geometry controls are uniform within each instance.
shape2d_polygon.usage: Use Distance Profile on Shape Distance to create bevels. Connect instance-scoped Cell Data to Seed for unique repeated outlines.
shape2d_polygon.notes: Radial and angular variation preserve vertex ordering. Spatially varying geometry controls clear metric distance. Transforms and warps follow the shared distance rules.

sides.title: Sides
sides.text: Vertex count, rounded and clamped to 3–16.

radius.title: Radius
radius.text: Circumradius of the regular outline in local UV units. Irregularity varies each vertex around this radius.

irregularity.title: Irregularity
irregularity.text: Seeded radial and angular vertex variation. Zero gives a regular polygon; vertex order is retained.

rotation.title: Rotation
rotation.text: Rotation of the complete outline in local degrees.

seed.title: Seed
seed.text: Deterministic outline variation. Connect instance-scoped Cell Data for a different outline per repeated item.

center.title: Center
center.text: Outline center in local UV coordinates.

smoothness.title: Union Smoothness
smoothness.text: Blend width used by Smooth Union when combining signed-distance shapes.

shape2d_star.title: Star
shape2d_star.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
shape2d_star.output: The preview shows the shape. Circle and Rounded Rectangle also provide signed distance as a separate connection choice; a grayscale shape result is not automatically material Opacity.
shape2d_star.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
shape2d_star.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

GRAD.title: Random Gradient
GRAD.text: Gives the shape a random gradient, useful for generating uneveness through visually tilting the shape.

globalScale.title: Global
globalScale.text: Global scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

localScale.title: Local
localScale.text: Local X/Y scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

offset.title: Offset
offset.text: X/Y offset of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the offset should be 0. as the pattern will position the shape automatically.

shape2d_tile.title: Tile
shape2d_tile.summary: Generates a tile shape. This is the default shape for brick and all other rectangular shaped patterns.
shape2d_tile.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
shape2d_tile.output: The preview shows the shape. Circle and Rounded Rectangle also provide signed distance as a separate connection choice; a grayscale shape result is not automatically material Opacity.
shape2d_tile.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
shape2d_tile.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

GRAD.title: Random Gradient
GRAD.text: Gives the shape a random gradient, useful for generating uneveness through visually tilting the shape.

globalScale.title: Global
globalScale.text: Global scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

localScale.title: Local
localScale.text: Local X/Y scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

offset.title: Offset
offset.text: X/Y offset of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the offset should be 0. as the pattern will position the shape automatically.

simplex.title: Simplex Noise
simplex.summary: Smooth simplex gradient noise with a character distinct from Perlin.
simplex.input: No image input is required. An optional input carries shape coverage.
simplex.output: A scalar noise value repeated in RGB, with incoming alpha preserved.
simplex.usage: Choose 2D or 3D, adjust feature size, then use fBm for layered detail.
simplex.notes: In the material preview, 3D is sampled as a slice. Changing Z Slice changes that slice; it does not switch the sphere to direct volume-texture evaluation.

globalScale.title: Scale
globalScale.text: Feature size. Increasing Scale enlarges the pattern.

localScale.title: Stretch XY
localScale.text: Feature-size multipliers along X and Y.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.text: 2D uses UV coordinates. 3D uses position coordinates and the selected Z slice.

slice.title: Z Slice
slice.text: Position of the sampled plane along Z. Used in 3D mode.

depthScale.title: Stretch Z
depthScale.text: Feature-size multiplier along Z. Used in 3D mode.

spots.title: Spots
spots.summary: Scattered soft blobs, rounded dots and pits with controllable size variation.
spots.input: No input image is required. Optional incoming alpha is preserved.
spots.output: A grayscale spot field repeated in RGB. Addition can accumulate values above one; Maximum retains the strongest spot.
spots.usage: Choose a Profile and Blend mode, then set Cells, Radius and Size Distribution. Use the result for pores, stains or height detail.
spots.notes: The source evaluates neighboring cells to find spots. Large radii and many dots per cell increase cost and can exceed the intended local coverage.

sys_normal.title: Normal
sys_normal.summary: Returns the normal supplied by the evaluation context.
sys_normal.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
sys_normal.output: Signed XYZ normal components, not an encoded normal-map color.
sys_normal.usage: Use only when the caller provides meaningful normals. Convert a height field with Height to Normal when you need a normal map.
sys_normal.notes: The standard 2D material bake supplies a fixed normal. This source does not read the sphere mesh normal at every shading point.

sys_position.title: Position
sys_position.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
sys_position.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
sys_position.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
sys_position.notes: The standard material bake samples a plane with a fixed Z value. Position is not direct access to every point on the preview sphere.

sys_texcoord2.title: Tex Coord 2D
sys_texcoord2.summary: Returns the current 2D texture UV coordinate.
sys_texcoord2.input: No input image is required. Properties can be controlled by row connections.
sys_texcoord2.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
sys_texcoord2.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
sys_texcoord2.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

trans_circularwarp.title: Circular Warp
trans_circularwarp.summary: Warps the input shape into circular rings.
trans_circularwarp.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
trans_circularwarp.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
trans_circularwarp.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
trans_circularwarp.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

trans_directional_blur.title: Directional Blur
trans_directional_blur.summary: A centered Gaussian directional blur that preserves colored cutout edges.
trans_directional_blur.output: Filtered straight RGBA; exact metric distance is cleared.
trans_directional_blur.usage: Set Radius in pixels or UV units, choose Direction in degrees and a sample count from 1–33.
trans_directional_blur.notes: Small compositions stay callable. Expensive inputs automatically become bounded intermediate GPU images with halo padding and premultiplied bilinear sampling. Downstream edits reuse input images; upstream edits invalidate them. Instance-dependent data cannot be cached across distinct instances.

units.title: Units
units.text: Pixels scales Radius by the current sampling footprint; UV uses document coordinate units.

samples.title: Samples
samples.text: Bounded count from 1–33; one samples the center only.

trans_linearwarp.title: Linear Warp
trans_linearwarp.summary: Linearly warps the input shapes into vertical stripes
trans_linearwarp.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
trans_linearwarp.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
trans_linearwarp.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
trans_linearwarp.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

trans_tiler.title: Grid
trans_tiler.summary: Repeats arbitrary RGBA rows in a seeded grid, including nested layouts and transparent shapes.
trans_tiler.input: Connect the row to repeat. Inside that row, Cell Data in Instance scope reports the current instance.
trans_tiler.output: Straight RGBA, with gaps and transformed upstream coverage; no metric distance survives repetition.
trans_tiler.usage: Use Cells, Gap and Row Stagger for layouts. Put a Transform inside the repeated row and connect its Rotation to Cell Data parity for alternating groups. Nested Grids give subcells independent keys.
trans_tiler.notes: Placement searches the nearest three columns in each of three rows after staggering. Jitter is limited to 0.45 cells and scale to one cell so this search remains bounded. Footprints are conservative; very dense/minified layouts are approximations, not a baked area average. Axis-aligned cells accumulate disjoint coverage to avoid alpha seams; overlapping rotated/jittered instances use ordered over compositing.

layout.title: Layout
layout.text: Cartesian repeats a rectangular grid. Rings varies sector counts with circumference to keep approximately constant strip width; Cells X is tangential density and Cells Y is radial density.

cells.title: Cells
cells.text: Positive integer cells per UV unit, rounded and clamped to 1–1024.

rowOffset.title: Row Stagger
rowOffset.text: Horizontal shift of alternating grid rows, measured in cell widths; 0.5 gives running bond.

gap.title: Gap
gap.text: Fraction of each cell reserved for empty space before instance scaling.

scale.title: Instance Scale
scale.text: Fractional size of each instance inside its available cell, limited to one.

rotation.title: Rotation
rotation.text: Base instance rotation in degrees. A row-controlled Transform inside the input row can use instance parity.

jitter.title: Jitter
jitter.text: Maximum seeded center displacement per axis, in cell units.

randomRotation.title: Random Rotation
randomRotation.text: Maximum seeded random angle added to Rotation, in degrees.

probability.title: Probability
probability.text: Probability that each instance is present; zero removes every instance.

seed.title: Seed
seed.text: Deterministic seed. Nested Grids also hash the parent identity to keep subcells independent.

transform.title: Transform
transform.summary: Scales, rotates and moves the input shape.
transform.input: Connect an upstream row to Image, or place this tile after a source in the same row. Properties can be controlled by separate row connections.
transform.output: RGB contains the resulting values. Use Source Channel on a connection to read one component; alpha is the fourth component.
transform.usage: Connect the result to another row or to a material input. Select a source channel and enable Remap when the receiving input needs a different range.
transform.notes: Alpha and material Opacity are separate: connect a mask to Opacity when the material needs transparent areas.

globalScale.title: Global
globalScale.text: Global scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

localScale.title: Local
localScale.text: Local X/Y scale of the shape. If shape is used inside a pattern the scale should be 1. as the pattern will scale the shape automatically.

voronoi.title: Voronoi
voronoi.summary: Seeded 2D or 3D cellular fields, with multiple distance metrics and exact Euclidean cell-border distance.
voronoi.input: UV in 2D or bake-context Position plus Z Slice in 3D. Optional image coverage is retained.
voronoi.output: Cell/F1/F2 remain RGB. Named connections also expose border, cell key, nearest site in document coordinates and local coordinates in feature units, independently of the visible Output menu.
voronoi.usage: Choose Metric for F1/F2. Choose Euclidean Border for cracks and cell edges, then shape the field using Levels or Compare/Select.
voronoi.notes: Distances are in feature-space units. Border uses bisector planes, not F2 minus F1, and always uses Euclidean geometry. A bounded complete search covers fully jittered sites in both dimensions.

globalScale.title: Scale
globalScale.text: Feature size. Increasing Scale enlarges the pattern.

localScale.title: Stretch XY
localScale.text: Feature-size multipliers along X and Y.

dimensions.title: Dimensions
dimensions.text: Choose UV sampling in 2D or position plus Z Slice in 3D.

slice.title: Z Slice
slice.text: Position of the sampled plane along Z. Used in 3D mode.

depthScale.title: Stretch Z
depthScale.text: Feature-size multiplier along Z. Used in 3D mode.

seed.title: Seed
seed.text: Deterministic seed. Nested Grids also hash the parent identity to keep subcells independent.

jitter.title: Jitter
jitter.text: Zero places a site at each cell center; one allows the full cell.

metric.title: Metric
metric.text: Euclidean, Manhattan or Chebyshev distance for F1/F2. Border always evaluates Euclidean geometry.

warp.title: Warp
warp.summary: Resamples an input row at displaced UV and 3D coordinates.
warp.input: Connect the row to distort. Vector displacement may come from another row.
warp.output: The image sampled at the displaced coordinates.
warp.usage: Self mode uses the input first channel as displacement. Vector mode uses the Vector property; center a 0–1 noise vector around zero for displacement in both directions.
warp.notes: Amount is a coordinate-space offset, not physical mesh displacement. Large offsets can disrupt seams or pull detail across neighboring cells.

wave_noise.title: Wave Noise
wave_noise.summary: Animated layered waves with a flowing, interference-like character.
wave_noise.input: No input image is required. Optional incoming alpha is preserved.
wave_noise.output: A grayscale field from a fixed twenty-layer wave construction.
wave_noise.usage: Adjust Scale and Stretch for the visible pattern. Time Offset selects the phase of the wave motion.
wave_noise.notes: The construction maps UV coordinates through a spherical parameterization. It is a complete wave source, not a general fBm operation, and can be more expensive than simple gradient noise.

white_noise.title: White Noise
white_noise.summary: Seeded independent random cell values with explicit UV density.
white_noise.input: No image input is needed. Optional alpha coverage is retained.
white_noise.output: Grayscale repeats one random value in RGB. Color returns independent RGB values.
white_noise.usage: Set Cells to control density and Seed for a new arrangement. Use low densities for random blocks or high densities for fine grain.
white_noise.notes: Cell density is independent of the preview pixel size. A single sample cannot represent every tiny cell when the pattern is heavily minified.

cells.title: Cells
cells.text: Number of random cells per UV unit along X and Y.

output.title: Output
output.text: Grayscale shares one value across RGB; Color uses independent components.

compose_channels.title: Compose Channels
compose_channels.summary: Builds an RGBA value from four independent scalar controls or row connections.
compose_channels.input: Connect scalar channels to X, Y, Z and Alpha independently.
compose_channels.output: RGB retains signed values; Alpha is clamped to 0–1.
compose_channels.usage: Use this to assemble packed fields, vectors, or a color plus an independently authored opacity.
compose_channels.notes: Selecting a channel on a wire extracts data; this tile assembles data from multiple rows.

levels.title: Levels
levels.summary: Remaps an explicit input range into an output range, with gamma and optional clamping.
levels.input: An image or scalar field, broadcast from its selected connection channel.
levels.output: Remapped RGB with incoming alpha retained.
levels.usage: Set Input Low/High to the actual source range, then Output Low/High. Gamma above one brightens the normalized midpoint.
levels.notes: Unclamped values use a signed power so negative input remains finite. Equal endpoints use a signed epsilon denominator.

curve.title: Curve
curve.summary: Shapes values through four fixed horizontal positions using straight segments or a monotone cubic.
curve.input: Normalized RGB or a selected scalar channel.
curve.usage: Adjust the values at zero, one third, two thirds and one. Choose Linear for corners or Monotone Cubic for smooth transitions.
curve.notes: Values outside 0–1 are clamped. Cubic interpolation preserves each segment’s monotonicity; it does not invent overshooting peaks.

distance_profile.title: Distance Profile
distance_profile.summary: Converts a signed distance into a reusable bevel, crown or height profile.
distance_profile.input: Choose Shape Distance on the connection from a Circle, Rounded Rectangle, or another row with valid distance.
distance_profile.output: Height in RGB, with the source coverage retained.
distance_profile.usage: Width is the inward bevel distance. Choose Linear, Smooth, Round or Concave, and scale with Height. Repeat the resulting row with Grid.
distance_profile.notes: Distance is negative inside. A distance connection now broadcasts automatically to image and vector inputs. Nonuniform transforms and warps invalidate exact metric distance.

normal_combine.title: Normal Combine
normal_combine.summary: Combines base and detail tangent-space normal maps using reoriented normal mapping.
normal_combine.input: Encoded RGB normal map, with flat normal (0.5, 0.5, 1).
normal_combine.output: Normalized encoded RGB normal, with the base alpha retained.
normal_combine.usage: Connect Detail Normal and set Detail Strength. Both normals must use the same tangent convention.
normal_combine.notes: Flip Y at Height to Normal when required. This is normal-map composition; it does not provide mesh geometry normals during a 2D bake.

vector_math.title: Vector Math
vector_math.summary: Length, distance, dot product, normalization, projection and XY rotation of vectors.
vector_math.input: RGB vector data; select and broadcast channels on the connection when needed.
vector_math.output: Length, Distance and Dot broadcast a scalar. Other operations return a vector. Alpha is retained.
vector_math.usage: Choose the operation, connect Other Vector when used, or set Angle in degrees for Rotate XY.
vector_math.notes: Rotating vector values does not resample the source image. Use Transform for coordinate rotation.

color_ramp.title: Color Ramp
color_ramp.summary: Maps the selected first channel through four ordered RGBA color stops.
color_ramp.input: A scalar field; choose the intended channel explicitly on its connection.
color_ramp.output: RGBA colors, with stop opacity multiplied by incoming coverage.
color_ramp.usage: Set stop positions and colors. Constant makes steps; Linear makes straight blends; Smooth eases each interval.
color_ramp.notes: Positions are kept at least 0.000001 apart in evaluation. Values outside the stop range use the endpoint color.

color1.title: Color 2
color1.text: First endpoint, as constant RGBA or a connected row.

color2.title: Color 3
color2.text: Second endpoint, as constant RGBA or a connected row.

coordinates.title: Coordinates
coordinates.summary: Cartesian, polar and cylindrical coordinate data, with 3D scaling, Euler rotation and translation. Connect XY or XYZ to a row's coordinate input. Angles use turns.
coordinates.input: UV and Position need no input. Input mode transforms connected vector data.
coordinates.output: Cartesian XYZ, polar (angle in turns, radius, Z) or cylindrical (angle in turns, radius, height).
coordinates.usage: Apply Scale, X/Y/Z Rotation in degrees, then Offset before mapping. Connect XY to a UV row, or XYZ to sample volume noise.
coordinates.notes: Row coordinate connections estimate a transformed footprint and accept XY or XYZ. Polar angles wrap at zero/one. Mapping clears metric distance; build a profile before deforming it when a constant world-space bevel is not required.

partition.title: Partition
partition.summary: Repeats RGBA in irregular intervals with shared boundaries, stable instance keys and normalized local coordinates.
partition.input: Connect an RGBA motif to repeat along irregular X or Y intervals.
partition.output: Image plus named key, local UV, center, width, bounds and random fields.
partition.usage: Cells controls interval density and Irregularity moves sites. Adjacent intervals share exact boundaries. Nest inside Grid for rows of varying-width bricks.
partition.notes: Jittered sites remain ordered. Width and Bounds are in document UV units. Instance keys stay stable under the local remapping.

scatter.title: Scatter
scatter.summary: Seeded overlapping RGBA stamps with multiple instances per cell, size/intensity variation, layers and Over/Add/Maximum blending.
scatter.input: Connect an RGBA motif in its local -0.5…0.5 support. Instance Cell Data remains available inside it.
scatter.output: Over composites RGBA. Add Height and Maximum Height combine alpha-weighted height/color contributions. Named fields expose the winning key, random value, angle and local UV.
scatter.usage: Choose Size, Instances per Cell, layers, size/intensity variation and Blend. Size can span up to three cells, with a bounded seven-by-seven search.
scatter.notes: Add/Maximum treat RGB as height fields and multiply by motif coverage. Per-instance controls belong inside the motif. Very dense minification is approximate; expensive motifs and high layer/instance counts remain bounded by compiler budgets.

height_gradient.title: Height Gradient
height_gradient.summary: Signed derivatives, slope and curvature from a height image.
height_gradient.input: The red channel is height; select another channel on the connection when needed.
height_gradient.output: Gradient XY with curvature in Z, or scalar slope/curvature. Named fields are independent of the visible Output mode.
height_gradient.usage: Feed Gradient XY to a vector displacement/filter. Remap signed curvature for edge and recess masks.
height_gradient.notes: Curvature is a finite-difference Laplacian, not ambient occlusion. Filtering radius controls the scale being measured. Expensive inputs use cached GPU passes.

radius.title: Radius
radius.text: Derivative sampling radius. Pixels clamp to at least 0.25; UV units support small physical sampling radii.

units.title: Units
units.text: Pixels follow the current sampling footprint. UV units retain a fixed document-space radius at different resolutions.

strength.title: Strength
strength.text: Signed multiplier for gradient and curvature. Negative values reverse their orientation/sign.

output.title: Output
output.text: Gradient returns signed XY derivatives with curvature in Z. Slope is gradient length; Curvature is the signed Laplacian. Named fields select these independently.

vector_filter.title: Vector Filter
vector_filter.summary: A bounded directional filter steered by a connected vector field.
vector_filter.input: RGBA image; red is the comparison height for Minimum and Maximum.
vector_filter.output: Selected RGBA for extrema, or premultiplied RGBA averaging. Metric distance is cleared.
vector_filter.usage: Use Height Gradient from a control noise as Vector. Minimum creates directional erosion; Maximum expands raised features.
vector_filter.notes: The local vector stays fixed along each sampling trail; this is not an iterative evolving flow solver. Vectors longer than one are normalized, shorter vectors reduce the travel distance. Expensive inputs use cached image passes.

mode.title: Mode
mode.text: Minimum or Maximum chooses a complete RGBA sample by red-channel height. Average filters premultiplied color and alpha.

radius.title: Radius
radius.text: Maximum trail travel in the chosen units, bounded to 0–64. Zero returns the original sample.

units.title: Units
units.text: Pixels follow the current sampling footprint; UV units retain a fixed document-space effect scale.

vector.title: Vector
vector.text: XY steers the trail. Vectors longer than one are normalized; shorter vectors shorten travel. Z is ignored.

samples.title: Samples
samples.text: Number of additional trail samples, bounded to 1–32. The center sample is always included.

centered.title: Centered
centered.text: Trail samples one direction from the starting point. Centered uses symmetric midpoint samples on both sides.
